title: Use AI to Scaffold Code, Then Make Tests Decide
subtitle: Accelerate the first implementation without treating generated code as reviewed code
description: Use AI to produce a first implementation for a bounded coding task, then inspect the diff, run tests, add missing edge cases, and reject code you cannot explain. A controlled experiment found faster completion on one coding task; it did not establish universal software quality gains.

lifeOsSource.hack: Let AI scaffold a bounded coding task, then require tests, diff review, and human explanation before accepting the change.
lifeOsSource.whatYouDo: Define the behavior and constraints first. Ask AI for a small implementation. Read the diff, run the existing test suite, add tests for edge cases and failure paths, and inspect security or data-handling implications. Keep only code you can explain and maintain.
lifeOsSource.checkIn: Did AI shorten implementation time without increasing code I do not understand, test, or want to own?
lifeOsSource.reference: Peng et al. (2023) — The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot

faq.question: What did the coding experiment show?
faq.answer: In a controlled experiment on a JavaScript HTTP-server task, developers with GitHub Copilot completed the task faster on average. It was a specific task and the result should not be generalized to every language, repository, or quality dimension.

faq.question: What is the minimum review?
faq.answer: Read the diff, run relevant tests, add missing edge cases, inspect dependencies and secrets, and understand the code path well enough to debug it later.

intro.html: Generated code can be fast to obtain and expensive to misunderstand. Use the speed; do not outsource the acceptance criteria.

sections.title: 1. Define behavior before code
sections.html: State inputs, outputs, failure behavior, constraints, and the tests that would convince you the task is complete. This gives the model less room to solve a different problem elegantly.

sections.title: 2. Generate a small change
sections.html: Prefer a reviewable diff over a repository-wide rewrite. Small generated changes are easier to test, explain, and revert.

sections.title: 3. Let executable checks disagree
sections.html: Run the existing suite and add edge cases the generated code may have missed. When tests and the explanation conflict, investigate instead of asking the model to sound more confident.

sections.title: 4. Keep only maintainable code
sections.html: Reject code you cannot explain, secure, or support. AI assistance changes how the code was drafted; it does not change who inherits the bug.

references.title: The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
references.claim_scope: In a controlled experiment on a specific JavaScript implementation task, participants with access to GitHub Copilot completed the task 55.8% faster on average. The evidence does not establish universal gains in code quality, security, maintainability, or performance across software work.

editorialCuration.reason: Keep the productivity signal narrow and pair it with ordinary software QA so generated code is treated as an implementation candidate, not a correctness proof.
